requirement:
`OutlineContent::outline` exposes the outline of its whole retained file,
including when the content value selects one item. The outline lists the file
root first, followed by its items in source preorder. Full selectors identify
items and their ancestry under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`.

```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
    pub fn outline(&self) -> &Outline;
}
```

The item's span includes its attached source under the language's rules. The
root has an empty selector and covers the entire source snapshot.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.outlines.items`. All tests are in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs`. I did not read implementation source.

- **Whole retained file, even when one item is selected.**
  - `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` builds content with `OutlineContent::from_id` for the second line of a three-item file. It asserts `selected.outline().items.len() == 3`, so the outline holds the whole file and not only the selected item.
  - That test also calls `selected.select("")` and checks that it returns the root with the full text.
  - `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` asserts `std::ptr::eq(function.outline(), contents.outline())` for a selected `fn`.
  - `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` asserts the same for a selected section.
- **Root first, with an empty selector, covering the entire source snapshot.**
  - The Rust test checks `selectors[0] == ""` and `items[0].span == Span::new(0, source.len())`.
  - The unknown-extension, Unicode and Markdown tests check the same, and the Unicode test also checks the root selector is empty.
  - `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` checks this for every bundled language.
  - The empty-source case gives a single root item with span `0..0`.
- **Items in source preorder with full ancestry selectors.**
  - The Rust test asserts the exact selector sequence `["", "mod[auth]", "mod[auth]/fn[check]", "mod[auth]/struct[Token]", "fn[last]"]`. A parent is followed by its children, then by the next sibling.
  - The Markdown tests assert nested section selectors in order, for example `main/section[Same]#1` before `#2`, and `section[End]/section[Level%20two]/block@…`.
  - The unknown-extension test asserts the order `alpha, beta, alpha` for line items.
- **Item spans include attached source.**
  - In the Rust test, the `fn check` span starts at the `/// Check tokens.` doc comment and includes `#[inline]`. It ends at the end of the function body.
  - The Markdown setext tests check that spans keep the original source offsets, including for items inside directives, lists and quotes.
  - Language-specific attachment rules belong to the `sources.*.items` requirements, so they are not assessed here.
- **Selector syntax details.** Selector encoding and the `#N` rules belong to `requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`, which this requirement only cites. Its own tests, together with the checks above, show the selectors are consistent.

I found no plausible requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.

The item's span includes its attached source under the language's rules. The
root has an empty selector and covers the entire source snapshot.
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
